question: May the Adaptive eligibility mode (dfs_eligibility) become the default for the NFL showdown tournament boards, in place of Conservative (today's depth-chart gate)?
sample: Every NFL showdown draft group the PC builds on its own (app._tourney_auto's showdown rule: a $500K+ GPP) whose inputs research/dfs_eligibility_record.py recorded BEFORE its lock, locking after this registration, through the 2026-27 playoffs; in lock order, the first n_target. DEN @ PIT (157076) is excluded (the development case). A slate not recorded before lock is not in the sample and is never backfilled; a recording the harness refuses (its universe or rule set not rebuilt) is not in it either.
per_slate: research/dfs_eligibility_compare.py on the recording, unchanged: 60,000 worlds from production's simulator (seed = the draft group id); worlds 0-29,999 choose each mode's top-1% ranking and its greedy 20-entry portfolio (dfs_tourney.greedy_cover on per-world top-1% indicators); worlds 30,000-59,999 only score them, against the conservative board's field at its per-world thresholds (dfs_evaluate's code, ties not split). d_s = P(any of adaptive's 20 entries in the top 1%) minus the same for conservative, on the independent worlds; cash_s the 20 entries' mean cash rate, adaptive minus conservative; d1_s the best single lineup's top-1% rate, the same difference.
primary: D = mean of d_s over the sample, SE = sd(d_s)/sqrt(n) over slates (each slate one observation; the within-slate paired SE is reported beside, never used). PASS when D > 0 and D > 2 SE.
noninferiority: mean(cash_s) + 2 SE >= 0 and mean(d1_s) + 2 SE >= 0: neither significantly worse.
read: Once: when the 12th sampled slate is recorded and scored, or on last_read_utc with whatever was recorded; fewer than n_min slates then is INCONCLUSIVE. research/dfs_eligibility_read.py is the read; before either condition it answers NOT READY and computes nothing.
decision: PASS on the primary and both non-inferiority checks: Adaptive MAY become the default, with the owner's sign-off. Anything else: Conservative stays. Slates where Adaptive admits nobody count as d_s = 0 (the rule's effect over the slates it runs on); the admitted-only subset is reported beside, descriptive. Unrestricted is reported beside, never decided here.
reported_never_decisive: each slate's real DraftKings points of each mode's #1 lineup and 20 entries (Sleeper's box, after the game) and, where the owner's standings export exists, their real finish; candidate counts, runtime and memory per mode.
not_covered: Classic: its comparison needs the whole classic board (field sampler, solves, portfolio) built per mode on the PC; it is registered separately once a classic harness exists. The house-rule audit is descriptive; lifting a rule is a separate decision.
power: Unknown before the first slates: DEN @ PIT gives one d_s (research/reports/dfs_eligibility.md); the between-slate spread is what decides power, and an inconclusive read is insufficient evidence, never evidence of no effect.

amendments.what: research/dfs_eligibility_compare.py gained the house-rule registration's two combined variants (lift:kdst_captain, lift:punts) and keeps each variant's 20 entries by name; the adaptive and conservative paths, the worlds, the choosing and the scoring are unchanged. No slate had been scored. The capture task (sd_capture) is now how recordings are made, before lock.

named the primary snapshot (primary_snapshot: lead) and made the read refuse any other; the primary snapshot is the LEAD look (sd_capture: 6 h to 2 h before lock), named before any slate is read (the owner: "designate which pre-lock snapshot is used for the primary research test in advance. We shouldn't retrospectively choose whichever snapshot produced better results"); it must have replayed exact. The close look (50 to 15 minutes before lock) and any hand recording are diagnostic only and never enter the primary read; a slate whose lead look is missing, refused or not exact is not in the sample (never replaced by its close look). The read scripts refuse any other label.
sd_capture.py: its numpy imports guarded by try/except ImportError (the suite's import rule); no behaviour change on the PC

primary_snapshot_rule: the primary snapshot is the LEAD look (sd_capture: 6 h to 2 h before lock), named before any slate is read (the owner: "designate which pre-lock snapshot is used for the primary research test in advance. We shouldn't retrospectively choose whichever snapshot produced better results"); it must have replayed exact. The close look (50 to 15 minutes before lock) and any hand recording are diagnostic only and never enter the primary read; a slate whose lead look is missing, refused or not exact is not in the sample (never replaced by its close look). The read scripts refuse any other label.
